ai.description: This 15–17 cm turtle has a brown, flat-topped carapace with three prominent longitudinal keels. The plastron is dark-blotched, and the head features a pointed snout and serrated posterior marginal scutes.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Keeled Box Turtle is uniquely identified by three prominent, serrated longitudinal keels on its carapace, which are absent in other similar Indian box or pond turtles.
ai.habitat: The Keeled Box Turtle inhabits humid, dense evergreen and deciduous forests in hilly terrain, typically at elevations between 200 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Keeled Box Turtle is primarily crepuscular and terrestrial, often remaining motionless among leaf litter to rely on its camouflaged, keeled shell for defense.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cuora mouhotii* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 1–5 eggs. Breeding occurs from May to August, with nesting taking place during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Keeled Box Turtle occurs in Northeast India, specifically in states like Assam and Mizoram, inhabiting forested hill regions at elevations up to 1,500 meters.
